Film/literary reception remains inside closest; support-only film rows do not generate an extra programme or skipped third.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both develop analysis of poems and narrative texts. UCR supplies sustained close-reading methods; the chronological Italian movements and authors remain distinct.

Both include language processing, acquisition and neurolinguistic questions. UCR concentrates on experimental/neurocognitive inquiry; the complete phonetics, phonology and structural linguistics survey remains broader at Leiden.

Comparative literary reading, genres, framed storytelling and historical contexts provide a direct formal relationship. The specific medieval French/Italian traditions and manuscript corpus are not reproduced.
Both examine literary transmission, intertextuality and cultural exchange. UCR focuses on comparative myth and Ovidian retelling; Leiden specifically studies Italian-English circulation.
Both analyze cinematic/literary narrative, film form and historical movement contexts. The dedicated Italian Neorealism corpus, theory and case studies remain distinct.
Both study literary transposition across media and the consequences of adaptation. UCR develops text-film interpretation; Italian-Dutch interlingual translation practice is not supplied.

Renaissance Italy and its Mediterranean/global artistic connections address an identifiable part of Italian cultural history and transnational exchange. Leiden covers the broader medieval/early-modern political and cultural history; the art course is not a full substitute.
Data preparation, textual/web data, analysis and visualization supply a specific part of digital-humanities practice. The wider platform, interface and AI-theory curriculum remains different.
UCR contributes stylistics, psycholinguistics and qualitative inquiry. Dedicated Italo-Romance history/contact, dialect structures and variationist sociolinguistics remain specialist gaps.

notes.text: This comparison assesses 170 documented EC. The missing 10 EC of restricted study and full later-cohort progression remain unverified. UCR offers sustained literary and language-analysis methods and Italian Renaissance cultural connections; advanced Italian proficiency, specialist Italian literary and linguistic study, and compulsory thesis training differ. Optional independent research is additional to its scheduled 180 EC.

audience.programmeDescription: Study Italian language, literature and culture through language practice, linguistic analysis, literary history, film and cultural-political history, with supervised research and approved open study.
audience.comparisonExplanation: This qualified comparison relates the documented Italian Studies curriculum to a broader UCR program in literary interpretation, language analysis and cultural inquiry, including Renaissance Italy. UCR offers substantial close reading, stylistics, adaptation and historical/visual research. It does not reproduce advanced Italian proficiency, the Italian literary canon, dialectology or the full regional curriculum. A complete Leiden degree pathway is not certified.

curriculum.limitation: The 24 distinct listed components total 170 EC, including 30 EC of approved open study. Repeated required modules are counted once. The remaining 10 EC of distinct restricted study and later-cohort entry and progression are unresolved; specific advanced-module and thesis eligibility are not certified.
